STEP 1 - Scene: Two halves of a cooked corn cob (sweet corn, kernels removed or eaten off, cob rings visible) on a white square plate. Photographed from directly above, roughly top-down.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 22 cm across the side (the plate is about 2/3 the width of the tray frame). Treat as a ~22 cm square; area ≈ 22 × 22 × ~0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 410 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: Two cob pieces (cut crosswise, each about 6 cm diameter, the rings are the cob cross-sections with kernels mostly gone), plus a few small yellow kernel fragments and crumbs on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Cob piece 1 ≈ 3.5% (about 28 cm² including its visible ring); cob piece 2 ≈ 4% (about 33 cm²); scattered kernel bits ≈ 0.5%. Total food coverage ≈ 8% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each cob piece is about 6 cm diameter by ~3 cm long (cut section of cob). Piece 1 ≈ 3.14 × 3² × 3 ≈ 85 ml as an envelope, but the hollow centre and missing kernels reduce it; using the outer envelope as instructed, ~85 ml. Piece 2 ≈ similar, ~85 ml. Kernel bits ≈ 3 ml. Total gross ≈ 173 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cob pieces are mostly fibrous core with few kernels; bulk density for cut vegetable pieces ~0.6 g/ml. Cob total ≈ 173 × 0.6 ≈ 104 g. Kernel bits: 3 × 0.6 ≈ 2 g. Total ≈ 106 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked sweet corn (kernels) ≈ 96 kcal/100 g. Most of the mass is cob core, which is low energy, so I use ~70 kcal/100 g as a blended value for cob with residual kernels. Cob pieces: 104 g × 70 / 100 ≈ 73 kcal. Kernel bits: 2 g × 96/100 ≈ 2 kcal. Total ≈ 75 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Two cob halves plus crumbs, about 100 g and roughly 75 kcal, is plausible for corn cob pieces with most kernels already eaten. The plate is largely empty, consistent with the low coverage estimate.
